job.name: Job
job.note: Upright man of Hus, father of ten grown children, stricken and lamenting.

1.t: The life of man upon earth is a warfare, and his days are like the days of a hireling.

2.t: As a servant longeth for the shade, as the hireling looketh for the end of his work;

3.t: So I also have had empty months, and have numbered to myself wearisome nights.

4.t: If I lie down to sleep, I shall say: When shall I rise? and again, I shall look for the evening, and shall be filled with sorrows even till darkness.

5.t: My flesh is clothed with rottenness and the filth of dust; my skin is withered and drawn together.

6.t: My days have passed more swiftly than the web is cut by the weaver, and are consumed without any hope.

7.t: Remember that my life is but wind, and my eye shall not return to see good things.

8.t: Nor shall the sight of man behold me: thy eyes are upon me, and I shall be no more.

9.t: As a cloud is consumed, and passeth away: so he that shall go down to hell shall not come up.

10.t: Nor shall he return any more into his house, neither shall his place know him any more

11.t: Wherefore, I will not spare my mouth, I will speak in the affliction of my spirit: I will talk with the bitterness of my soul.

12.t: Am I a sea, or a whale, that thou hast enclosed me in a prison?

13.t: If I say: My bed shall comfort me, and I shall be relieved, speaking with myself on my couch:

14.t: Thou wilt frighten me with dreams, and terrify me with visions.

15.t: So that my soul rather chooseth hanging, and my bones death.

16.t: I have done with hope, I shall now live no longer: spare me, for my days are nothing.

17.t: What is a man, that thou shouldst magnify him or why dost thou set thy heart upon him?

18.t: Thou visitest him early in the morning, and thou provest him suddenly.

19.t: How long wilt thou not spare me, nor suffer me to swallow down my spittle?

20.t: I have sinned: what shall I do to thee, O keeper of men? why hast thou set me opposite to thee. and am I become burdensome to myself?

21.t: Why dost thou not remove my sin, and why dost thou not take away my iniquity? Behold now I shall sleep in the dust: and if thou seek me in the morning, I shall not be.
